public_rationale: The reviewed disclosures do not verify the combined $448 billion and 50% assertion. They report different company and contract scopes without a matching two-customer breakdown. Microsoft's reported growth excluding OpenAI also cautions against the broader weak-demand inference, but does not settle demand excluding both customers across hyperscalers. public_payload.normalized_proposition: Demand for compute beyond OpenAI and Anthropic is not large; they make up 50% of hyperscaler RPOs ($448B).

statement.excerpt: Nevertheless, said demand can’t be that large, otherwise we’d A) have other companies trying to build their own compute (other than Poolside, which failed to raise money to do so) and B) massive remaining performance obligations — hundreds of billions of dollars’ worth — rather than the grim truth that 50% of hyperscaler RPOs are from Anthropic and OpenAI, inflating obligations by $448 billion

from_speaker: said demand can’t be that large
50% of hyperscaler RPOs are from Anthropic and OpenAI
our_interpretation: The numerical proposition is that OpenAI and Anthropic together account for approximately half of the relevant hyperscalers' outstanding performance obligations, totaling approximately USD 448 billion.
The surrounding discussion names Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. I use those as the provisional comparison set, while preserving the uncertainty about whether another set was intended.

For this ongoing financial observation, I use March 31, 2026: the latest common quarter-end ordinarily covered by public quarterly reports before July 7. This is a stock of outstanding obligations, not quarterly revenue.
The supplied passage does not identify whether the combined customer attribution is company-reported or an external estimate. The contract's accounting basis therefore remains unknown.
Not large has no numerical demand threshold. Concentration alone does not establish that the remaining absolute demand is small, or distinguish AI compute from other cloud services.
criteria.support_condition: A reconciliation for the same date, company set, accounting treatment, and contract scope establishes approximately USD 448 billion of recognized outstanding obligations attributable to the two customers and approximately a 50% share. Separate evidence establishes the claimed small scale of other compute demand.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A matching reconciliation establishes a materially different customer amount or share, or comparable evidence establishes substantial other compute demand under an identified threshold. No supported or contradicted score is permitted while the contract's accounting basis remains unknown.
